_source: Forge-C factory/checklists/v0.4/SWE.2.yaml and the inherited v0.3 factory/release-manager/checklists/SWE.2.yaml, neutralised for feature 023

items.title: Requirement allocation complete
items.pass_criterion: Every requirement of the level above is allocated to at least one software element, and the architecture references no unknown requirement ID.
items.typical_defect: A requirement allocated to no element, or an allocation to a non-existent requirement ID.

items.title: Elements and interfaces identified
items.pass_criterion: Every software element has a unique ID and defined responsibility; every connection between elements carries a unique interface ID.
items.typical_defect: Unnamed connection between elements, or two elements sharing one ID.

items.title: Well-formed workproduct and views
items.pass_criterion: The workproduct is the architecture itself (not a status summary), contains element, interface, hardware-resource and requirement-allocation sections, and its static and dynamic views use a machine-checkable notation that parses and renders.
items.typical_defect: A status reply submitted as the architecture, or a view that fails to parse.

items.title: Dynamic behaviour specified
items.pass_criterion: The dynamic view shows operating modes, main interaction sequences of the allocated interfaces, and error/timeout paths for blocking operations (or the caller-bounded wait where the element itself does not time out).
items.typical_defect: Sequence shows only the success path; no timeout or error path for a blocking call.

items.title: Hardware resource ownership and access semantics
items.pass_criterion: Ownership of shared hardware resources, access semantics (volatile, atomic or read-modify-write), clock and reset dependencies are defined, and every hardware fact matches the controlled hardware reference supplied as input.
items.typical_defect: Two elements write the same register field with no owner; offset not found in the hardware reference.

items.title: Concurrency and scheduling addressed
items.pass_criterion: Concurrency, interrupt/event synchronisation, scheduling and reentrancy of elements and interfaces are addressed.
items.typical_defect: Shared state accessed from interrupt and task context with no synchronisation stated.

items.title: Safety mechanisms and degraded states
items.pass_criterion: Where integrity requirements apply, safety mechanisms, degraded states, fault reactions and architectural dependencies (including freedom from interference) are defined and allocated to elements.
items.typical_defect: Allocated diagnostic requirement with no element or mechanism realising it.

items.title: Resource budgets allocated
items.pass_criterion: Memory and timing budgets are allocated across elements and justified against the allocated constraints.
items.typical_defect: No stack/RAM/time budget per element, or budgets that exceed the allocated limit.

items.title: Decisions and trace consistent
items.pass_criterion: Architecture decisions are recorded with rationale, and the bidirectional trace between requirements and elements is consistent in meaning, not only in links.
items.typical_defect: Element linked to a requirement whose behaviour it does not provide.

items.title: Abstraction layers separated
items.pass_criterion: Where the design is layered (e.g. low-level hardware access vs. higher-level service API), each layer is a separate element with defined interfaces between layers.
items.typical_defect: Low-level hardware access and service API merged in one element with no interface between them.
